1. Labels $y_i$ (only features $x_i$ are given).
2. Clustering and dimensionality reduction (density / representation learning also count).
3. Lower $d$ can cut noise, cost, and overfitting, or aid visualization.
4. No: classification predicts known classes; clustering invents groups without $y$.
5. Contrastive learning / NCE-style methods (e.g. SimCLR), or autoencoders / PCA as classical cases.
